title: Introducing Shadermix
excerpt: An open-source library of shader backgrounds for Astro and Webflow — framework-free, zero dependencies.

children.text: Most of the good component libraries are React-only. If you build marketing sites in Astro or Webflow, adding a shader background usually means shipping a React runtime for something that is, in the end, one fullscreen quad and a fragment shader.
Shadermix is the alternative: effects written once in plain TypeScript and WebGL, shipped to Astro, Webflow, and plain JavaScript.

What makes it different
Zero runtime dependencies — no three.js, no ogl, no GSAP.
Pauses offscreen and in hidden tabs; caps device pixel ratio.
Respects prefers-reduced-motion and falls back to a CSS gradient without WebGL.
MIT licensed, with original shaders — nothing lifted from ShaderToy.
Where it is going

The first release targets ten effects that look great rather than fifty that look fine. After that: a CLI for copy-paste installs, more effects weekly, and page blocks and templates for both Astro and Webflow.

title: Introduction
description: What Shadermix is and why it exists.

children.text: Shadermix is an open-source library of animated shader backgrounds, visual effects and text animations for Astro and Webflow. Every effect is written once in plain TypeScript and WebGL with zero runtime dependencies, then shipped three ways.
How it ships
Astro — native .astro components, no React or Vue runtime.
Webflow — one script tag from a CDN plus custom attributes on any div.
Vanilla JS — createAurora(canvas, options) for any other site.
Principles

Every component follows the same rules: zero runtime dependencies, pause when offscreen or when the tab is hidden, respect prefers-reduced-motion, and fall back to a CSS gradient when WebGL is unavailable.

title: Install in Astro
description: Add Shadermix effects to an Astro project.

children.text: Install
Usage
Import the component you need and drop it into any .astro file:

body.code:
--- import { Aurora } from '@shadermix/astro'; ---

Ship beautiful sites

children.text: Layering content
The effect renders a canvas positioned absolutely inside its host element. Put your content in a sibling element with position: relative and z-index: 1 so it sits above the canvas.

body.code:
.hero { position: relative; min-height: 60vh; }
.sm-content { position: relative; z-index: 1; }

children.text: View Transitions
Shadermix components initialise on astro:page-load and destroy on astro:before-swap, so they work with and without Astro's ClientRouter. No extra configuration is needed.
Copy-paste instead of npm
Every component page has a Source tab with the full shader and factory source. Drop those files into src/components/shadermix/ if you would rather own the code than depend on the package.

title: Install in Webflow
description: Add Shadermix effects to a Webflow site with one script tag.

children.text: Add the script
In Site Settings → Custom Code → Footer code, paste:
Pinning the major version (@0) means you get fixes automatically without breaking changes.
Use an effect
Select a Section or Div Block and give it a min height.
In Element Settings → Custom Attributes, add sm-effect with a value like aurora.
Add optional attributes such as sm-colors and sm-speed.
Put your content in a child div with class sm-content.
Publish or open Preview — custom code does not run on the Designer canvas.
Attributes
Attribute names are the kebab-case form of each option, prefixed with sm-. A colors option becomes sm-colors and takes a comma-separated list.
CMS and dynamic content

If you add elements after page load — CMS load-more, tabs, sliders — call window.Shadermix.init() to initialise any new elements. Already-initialised elements are marked with sm-ready and are never double-initialised.

Controlling an effect
You can pass either a canvas element or a container. If you pass a container, Shadermix creates a canvas that fills it and sets position: relative on the host if needed.
From a CDN
The Webflow bundle works on any site — it registers every effect and initialises elements carrying sm-effect attributes.

title: Performance
description: How Shadermix keeps effects cheap, and how many to use per page.

children.text: Shader backgrounds are easy to get wrong. Shadermix applies the same performance rules to every effect so you do not have to think about them.
What every effect does
Pauses when scrolled out of view, via IntersectionObserver.
Pauses when the browser tab is hidden.
Caps device pixel ratio at 2, so 3x displays do not render 9x the pixels.
Draws a single fullscreen quad per frame — no scene graph, no per-object overhead.
Shares one requestAnimationFrame loop across every effect on the page.
Reduced motion
When prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is set, effects render one static frame and never start the animation loop. Pass respectReducedMotion: false to override this, but prefer not to.
How many per page?

Browsers cap the number of simultaneous WebGL contexts, typically around 16. Shadermix warns in the console if a page creates more than 8 live contexts. For a gallery of previews, start effects only when a card is visible and hovered, and destroy them when it leaves the viewport — that is exactly what the components gallery on this site does.
When WebGL is unavailable

If the browser cannot create a WebGL context, or the context is lost and not restored, the host element falls back to a CSS gradient built from the same colors you configured. Content stays readable either way.

title: First three effects and the runtime

children.text: The core runtime and the first three background effects are in place. Nothing is published to npm yet — this entry tracks development progress.
aurora — soft flowing northern-lights bands.
mesh-gradient — slowly morphing multi-point colour mesh.
grain-gradient — animated angled gradient with film grain.
The runtime handles resize and device pixel ratio, pausing offscreen and in hidden tabs, reduced-motion fallbacks, WebGL context loss, and a shared animation loop across every effect on a page.
